review_type: single AI curator; full received final answer read; model identity visible

errors.quote: Apply the inverse factor to all enzymatic data
errors.issue: The defined factor is f = F_without/F_with. Correcting attenuation requires multiplying the background-corrected signal by f, not its inverse. For 100 versus 50 RFU, f=2; the stated inverse gives 25 instead of restoring 100. This reverses the central correction.

errors.quote: Any drop in fluorescence here is purely optical (no reaction occurs).
errors.issue: Absence of enzymes does not exclude compound–fluorophore chemical reaction or destruction. Independent analyte integrity/recovery is needed.

errors.quote: competitive inhibition at the target active site
errors.issue: Competitive kinetics do not by themselves identify an active-site interaction. Allosteric and substrate-availability mechanisms can mimic the pattern.

errors.quote: If reporter-only velocity is unaffected after correction → the reporter path is clean and any remaining signal loss is attributable to the target.
errors.issue: Reporter equivalence must be established at relevant intermediate concentrations; substrate/product loss and matrix effects remain possible. No adequate orthogonal product recovery or no-enzyme chemical-fate validation is specified.
The categorical aggregation diagnosis is not justified: detergent can alter free inhibitor, target conformation or readout. Compatibility and independent aggregation evidence are necessary.

rationale: The right modules are named, including an orthogonal target assay, but the explicitly inverted correction factor would exaggerate the artifact. Further chemical-versus-optical and binding-site overclaims undermine the proposed decision chain. Plate blocking and global fitting help, yet do not repair those central issues.
reference_guardrails: D3 establishes spectral proximity, not the magnitude of inner filtering. Fluorophore-only signal loss does not distinguish absorption, quenching and chemical conversion.
Substrate-competitive inhibition is a kinetic subclass of target inhibition; it is not necessarily active-site occupancy. Substrate sequestration and chemical loss require separate controls.
Reporter-only inhibition and true target inhibition can coexist. Do not force mutually exclusive categories or subtract arbitrary effect percentages.

A fully validated staged reporter calibration can be informative; a specific analytical instrument is not mandatory. Target quenching, matrix matching, product recovery and chemical stability must justify the inference.
Orthogonal methods can have their own compound-dependent artifacts, including ion suppression. Nonfluorescence alone does not establish specificity.
Independent preparations/days support reproducibility; technical wells cannot substitute for them. A null significance test is not equivalence; margins should be scientifically justified.
Simple inner-filter correction formulas depend on optical geometry. For f=F_without/F_with, attenuation correction multiplies signal by f, not by 1/f.

The draft reference uses reporter Km as a preparation item, but full reporter Michaelis-Menten characterization is not universally essential if empirical capacity and relevant intermediate concentrations are validated.

No fixed concentrations, replicate counts, Z-prime or R-squared thresholds are supplied by the packet. Proposed pilot settings are acceptable when labeled and validated; they are not historical facts.
